evidence.text: Q3 2026 PC unit shipments fell 20.1% YoY (IDC, Oct 8) to 22.4% (Gartner, Oct 12) on memory-cost-driven price rises, and Omdia/Counterpoint forecast another 24-27% decline in Q4. Corsair's FY guide still implies a Q4 of about $431M revenue and about $40M adj EBITDA, down only about 1% YoY on revenue. Its Gaming Components & Systems segment (63% of Q2 revenue) is guided to decline low double digits. The risk lands on the FY/Q4 guide, the line that sank last year's Q3 print.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q3 2025 (2025-11-04): revenue miss plus a lowered full-year guide, stock -13.16% (baseline; https://www.itiger.com/news/1192909105). Q2 2026 raised the FY guide and the stock rose +35.25%; Q4 2025 guided FY26 EBITDA growth and it rose +48.25%. This name moves hard on the FY range.
evidence.why_not_priced: Corsair has not spoken since Aug 6, before these Q3 unit data and the Q4 forecasts were published, so the FY range has not been tested against them. If the market had priced a Q4 cut, puts would be bid. Instead skew is -11.9 (calls bid) and put/call OI is 0.21. The 5-day -7.7% drift is the only sign of it.
evidence.independence: This is a proxy: OEM PC units are not Corsair's DIY channel, and IDC attributes part of the drop to early-2026 stockpiling, which may not apply to DIY. Same direction: IDC preliminary 20.1% (https://pasqualepillitteri.it/en/news/22264/pc-shipments-fall-20-1-idc) and Logitech's CEO citing a 20% fall in PC shipments (https://www.tikr.com/blog/logitech-sinks-11-on-weak-holiday-guidance-as-chip-supplier-incident-bites-fortunately-q3-carries-the-brunt). Offsetting [sizing note removed]: the peripherals segment (37%) is guided up low double digits, and memory revenue rises with ASP (+17% YoY in Q2). The size is net of those.

evidence.text: Logitech's Q2 FY27 (quarter to Sep 30, released Oct 27) grew sales 3% to $1.22B, its 11th straight growth quarter, with Gaming a named growth driver and mice/keyboards up mid-single digits while PC shipments fell 20%. Peripheral end-demand held through September, which bears on Corsair's peripherals segment (guided +low double digits for Q3).
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Corsair peripherals beat in Q1 (+10%) and Q2 (+13%) of 2026, and the stock rose +11.1% and +35.3% on those prints. Peripherals fell in Q4 2025 and the stock still rose +48% on margin and guide.
evidence.why_not_priced: A peer's quarter reported after Corsair last spoke, so Q3 consensus ($332-343M) was set before it. But Logitech fell 11-12% on its holiday guide, so read-through sentiment was negative, not positive. CRSR's 5-day -7.7% is consistent with sympathy selling, not with having priced healthy Q3 peripheral demand.
evidence.independence: Shares a document set with the supplier-incident finding (Logitech's Oct 27 release), but these are different facts: demand here, supply there. Supporting: https://www.tikr.com/blog/logitech-sinks-11-on-weak-holiday-guidance-as-chip-supplier-incident-bites-fortunately-q3-carries-the-brunt (mice and keyboards grew mid-single digits).

evidence.text: Logitech disclosed that an unnamed semiconductor supplier's plant closed at the end of June after a serious incident, reopened in September, and is still below required capacity. Logitech's Dec-quarter guide carries a $70-80M sales hit (it warned of up to $200M in July), and its stock fell 11-12%. Corsair did not mention any supplier problem on its Aug 6 call, and its exposure to the same supplier is unknown.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior Corsair supply-disruption print in the baseline window; the 2025-11-04 guide cut (-13.2%) is the nearest analogue on the guidance line.
evidence.why_not_priced: If the market believed Corsair shared the supplier, CRSR would have gapped with LOGI on Oct 28 and puts would be bid. The skew instead pays for upside.
evidence.independence: Same Logitech release as the demand finding. Second source on the incident: https://247wallst.com/cards/logitech-q2-2027-earnings-logi-01m5zg0kygyhbj99fgs2mqk5vc. Nothing ties it to Corsair, so this is an inference with no confirmation.

evidence.text: Retail DDR5 kit prices kept rising through Q3: a mainstream 32GB DDR5 kit starts about $350-450 in October 2026, against about $100-200 a year earlier (Tom's Hardware RAM price index; Newegg $399-479). Corsair's memory revenue was +17% YoY in Q2 on ASP and North American share gains, with supply 'adequate'. A memory module maker's Q3 revenue rises with kit ASP, pointing to components revenue at or above the 'declines low double digits' guide. TrendForce's Q4 contract increase slows to about +20% QoQ from about 80%/40%, and management already guided memory gross margin down to the high teens in Q4.
evidence.source_date: 2026-10-14 (price observation as quoted in search snippet; snippet_only, page not fetched)
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q4 2025 memory +24% drove a components beat and the stock rose +48.25%. Q2 2026 memory +17% and the stock rose +35.25% (with the guide raise).
evidence.why_not_priced: The Q3 guide was set Aug 6, assuming a components decline. Retail kit prices rose further after that, so consensus revenue ($332-343M) brackets the guide midpoint rather than above it. If priced, consensus would sit near the top of the $320-350M range.
evidence.independence: A proxy (retail price series, not Corsair's own number). Newegg insider, Oct 2026: https://www.newegg.com/insider/?p=93717. Against it: unit demand destruction (DDR5 kits sitting on shelves, https://www.tweaktown.com/news/110989/ddr5-memory-and-ssds-sit-on-retail-shelves-as-128gb-kit-prices-hit-4-200/index.html) and an early European retail decline report, which risks an inventory margin squeeze. Sized net of both.

evidence.text: The company itself scheduled an initial 2027 outlook for the combined Grindr + Freddie (PurposeMed) for this Q3 call, so this print carries a first guide for a new year. Freddie's 2026 revenue is expected above $80M with adj. EBITDA above $10M (about 12.5% margin), against Grindr's FY26 guide of about $540M revenue and about $232M adj. EBITDA at roughly 43%. So the combined 2027 headline revenue should land well above the $592M-$617M aggregator 2027 figures, which most likely exclude Freddie. The combined margin will be diluted below the 39-42% long-term target the company reaffirmed. The core-growth guide is the unknown.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 raised the FY guide by $5M on a 4.3% revenue beat and the stock fell 3.3% (baseline). In Q3 2025 the revenue guide was reaffirmed, EBITDA guidance was raised, and the stock rose 11.0%. In Q1 2026 the guide was raised to $535M and the stock rose 9.3% (baseline). Guidance direction has decided the sign.
evidence.why_not_priced: No published 2027 consensus includes Freddie; the aggregator 2027 figures ($592M-$617M) predate or ignore it. If the market had priced a margin-dilutive combined guide, previews would quote a combined 2027 number. Instead the Oct 28 preview frames 2027 only as Edge versus a growth fade and does not mention Freddie.
evidence.independence: The press release in the same 8-K (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1820144/000182014426000033/exhibit991-pressreleasedat.htm) says the same, so it is one document family. The Nov 2 8-K (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1820144/000182014426000036/grnd-20261102.htm) confirms the deal closed on Nov 2, so Freddie consolidates from Q4. The sign is my inference: a company that chooses to give an early outlook is usually comfortable with it.

evidence.text: Q3 revenue consensus is $136.4M-$136.6M, below Q2 2026's reported $138.1M. That is a sequential decline and only +17.8% year on year against Q3 2025's $115.8M. Q2 showed average paying users of 1.4M (+16% YoY) and ARPPU of $26.51 (+12%), and management wrote it is 'performing ahead of what we expected coming into the year'. The last three revenue prints beat: Q2 2026 by 4.3% ($138.1M vs $132.4M), Q3 2025 by 2.2% ($115.8M vs $113.3M). A Q3 at merely flat sequential revenue ($138M) would beat by about 1.2%. A Q3 2025-style sequential gain would beat by 3-5%.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Revenue beats have bought mixed reactions. Q3 2025's 2.2% beat bought +11.0%; Q2 2026's 4.3% beat was sold (-3.3% in the baseline, -6.7% after hours per one recap). This name does not reliably pay for a beat.
evidence.why_not_priced: A consensus below the prior quarter's revenue means the Street has taken management's flat-H2 guide literally. If the market expected a beat, previews would carry a whisper above $138M, and the stock would not sit 18% below the last print near its post-earnings low.
evidence.independence: Earnings Whispers preview (https://www.earningswhispers.com/article/GRND/22297, 2026-10-28) for the bar. Q3 2025 beat history: https://www.itiger.com/news/2581046171. The Q2 beat size comes from aggregator search results. Management guided to H2 deceleration as 2025 price increases lap, which caps the size.

evidence.text: Grindr agreed on 2026-09-02 to settle the UK privacy group action for GBP 26M (about $35M): GBP 13M due by 2026-12-31 and GBP 13M by 2027-03-31. The Q2 10-Q showed only $2.6M of accrued legal contingencies at June 30, so most of the charge should hit Q3 GAAP results, about $0.15-0.20 a share before any tax effect, against a $0.16 EPS consensus. Grindr adds back litigation costs in adj. EBITDA, so the guided EBITDA line is unaffected.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 GAAP EPS was reported as a miss ($0.10 vs $0.15-0.16 per aggregators) alongside a revenue beat, and the stock fell 3.3%. That GAAP-line reaction cannot be separated from the guide.
evidence.why_not_priced: Whether the $0.16 consensus includes the charge is not visible. If it did, previews would show Q3 EPS well below the year-ago $0.16 rather than 'flat with the year-ago quarter'. The charge has no path to the guide, so it is sized as a headline-only item.
evidence.independence: The Hacker News, 2026-09-08 (https://thehackernews.com/2026/09/grindr-to-pay-26-million-to-settle-uk.html), gives the $35.1M figure. The accrual of $2.6M at June 30 comes from the Q2 10-Q (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1820144/000182014426000025/grnd-20260630.htm).

evidence.text: Grindr had $6.5M of cash at 2026-06-30, a $390M term loan, and an undrawn $200M revolver. It paid $190M in cash for PurposeMed at the Nov 2 close and owes GBP 26M of settlement payments by March 2027. So net debt rises to roughly $560M+, about 2.4x the FY26 adj. EBITDA guide, and buybacks are already 'more opportunistic'. The money buys a business with revenue above $80M that adds EBITDA dollars, so the sign is near zero.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior print turned on leverage. The stock fell 4.3% on the day of the deal announcement, before it was public, and moved little after (Stocktwits).
evidence.why_not_priced: The deal terms are public, and the funding route (a revolver draw or new debt) and the hit to buyback capacity will first be shown in the Q3 letter and balance sheet. If the market had priced it, the stock would have reacted to the deal more than it did.
evidence.independence: The Nov 2 8-K confirms the $190M of cash paid at close (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1820144/000182014426000036/grnd-20261102.htm). The Q2 letter says buybacks are more opportunistic and about $300M remains authorized.

evidence.text: Beta Bionics, a direct US pump competitor, reported on 2026-10-27. It quantified up to $8.5M of Q4 2026 revenue it may lose as prospective pump users wait for its tubeless Mint (cleared 2026-09-14, full launch Q1 2027). Its pharmacy-benefit channel sales rose 118% y/y while DME rose only 4%. For Tandem the deferral is the risk: its own Mobi tubeless is promised for a 'scaled launch in H2 2026'. If buyers wait for it, the same deferral hits Tandem's implied Q4 US sales of $210-225M (flat to +7% y/y), which the FY guide needs. The pharmacy surge supports Tandem's pharmacy-led US ramp, so I net the two at a small negative.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: TNDM has moved on the guide and the pharmacy narrative more than on the quarter. Q2 2026 sales of $254.6M slightly missed the ~$255M guide and the stock rose 19.1%, on the FY reaffirmation and pharmacy progress. Q4 2025 issued a 'cautious' 2026 guide and the stock rose 32.7%. Q1 2026 fell 16.2%.
evidence.why_not_priced: No Tandem preview found in the search connects a peer's quantified wait-for-tubeless deferral to Tandem's Q4 implied guide. If the market had priced it, street revenue would sit at or below the $265M guide, not $266-271M above it. TNDM in fact rallied from $17.43 to $19.79 in the week after the BBNX release (Yahoo chart).

evidence.text: Management said on the Q2 call (2026-08-06) that the Mobi tubeless 510(k) was submitted in Q2 and that a scaled launch would follow clearance in H2 2026, with 2027 the first full year. openFDA's 510(k) records list Tandem's latest decision as K260429 (Control-IQ+, 2026-04-24) and show no tubeless clearance. With under two months of 2026 left, the call is at risk of pushing the scaled launch into 2027, or of having to explain the timing. The other possibility is that the clearance is announced with the print, which would be a positive surprise.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior print has resolved tubeless timing. Pipeline milestones (Mobi Android, Libre 3 integration) were part of the narrative on the +19.1% Q2 print.
evidence.why_not_priced: openFDA posts with a lag of a few weeks, so the absence is only suggestive. No press release or 8-K announced a clearance (EDGAR shows no 8-K since 2026-08-06). If a slip were priced, sell-side previews would carry a 2027 tubeless timeline; the search found none dated after August.
evidence.independence: Management's timing is in the Q2 call transcript (https://www.webull.com/news/15734772929471488). The FDA-database absence is the only evidence of delay, and it is subject to the database's lag.
